name: Peer-to-peer rental index: consumer GeForce (4090 / 3090 / 5090 per-GPU-hour)
region: global (16-17 host countries observed per SKU)
price_basis: USD per GPU-HOUR for the GPU component, verified peer-to-peer hosts, 1-GPU bundles, observed 2026-10-03. Asking rental rate, NOT a realised rental. GeForce cards, not datacenter parts - kept as a separate record so consumer and datacenter bands never mix.
notes:
OBSERVATION DATE 2026-10-03. Source sup-price-vast-rental-api. THREE DISTINCT BANDS, all observed 2026-10-03, all per-GPU-hour on 1-GPU verified hosts: RTX 4090 n=43, range $0.3024-$0.9356, median $0.4289; RTX 5090 n=41, range $0.4015-$0.7356, median $0.4896; RTX 3090 n=32, range $0.1213-$0.2523, median $0.1498. price_usd records the RTX 4090 median only because the schema has one price slot and 4090 has both the largest sample (n=43) and the tightest spread; the other two medians are carried in notes. THE SEGMENT BOUNDARY, stated as a number: the RTX 3090 rents at ~0.35x the RTX 4090 rate ($0.1498/$0.4289 = 0.35) while its asking PURCHASE price is ~0.46x ($1,514/$3,299 medians, sup-price-picclick-ebay-asking). Rental and purchase price do not move together across these SKUs, which is the practical reason neither number can stand in for the other. Sample sizes here (32-43 per SKU) are large enough that these medians are the most statistically solid figures in this entire slice.

 EXPORT CONTROL (2026-10-04, mechanism-level; source spl-eccn-3a090-ccl): consumer gaming cards of this generation generally do NOT meet the 3A090.a TPP/performance-density parameters and fall under ECCN 3A001 or are designated EAR99, i.e. the advanced-computing licence regime with its case-by-case and D:5 screening does not attach to them. This is exactly what makes export status a PER-PART property rather than a per-vendor one: a GeForce RTX 5090 and a datacenter/professional part from the same vendor and the same process generation can carry entirely different control status. Recorded as false for that reason, NOT because the part is unregulated - it remains subject to the EAR generally, to destination-country import rules, and to screening of the consignee and its ultimate parent against the Entity, Unverified and MEU lists (15 CFR part 744). The binding ECCN determination for any specific SKU is the exporter's own classification, which no public vendor page states.

 LEAD TIME: null - and specifically because a PEER-TO-PEER marketplace has no lead time at all. Host nodes appear and disappear, so the availability a buyer sees is a snapshot of what some host posted on the observation date, not a schedulable delivery date. This is the widest availability uncertainty in the whole supply set and it is structural rather than a missing datum: it argues directly for the renting-over-buying decision this record feeds. Probe log in source spl-negative-no-oem-publishes-lead-time.
